nodes.name: NF Cleaning
nodes.procedure: nickel foam (NF) (20 mm×20 mm×0.42 mm) was cleaned by sequential treatment with 2 M HCl solution, ethanol, and deionized water for 10 min.
nodes.source_text: nickel foam (NF) (20 mm×20 mm×0.42 mm) was cleaned by sequential treatment with 2 M HCl solution, ethanol, and deionized water for 10 min.

nodes.name: NiFe-LDH Electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: NF was used as the working electrode, a graphite rod was used as the counter electrode, and a saturated calomel electrode (SCE) was used as the reference electrode. The electrolyte was a mixture of 9 mM Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and 3 mM Fe(NO3)3·9H2O. A constant cathodic current of 2 mA/cm² was applied to the working electrode for 1 h. The product coated on NF was cleaned thoroughly using ethanol and distilled water several times and dried in an oven at 60°C for 12 h, and the pristine NiFe-LDH sample was obtained.

nodes.name: W-doping Corrosion (parallel variants)
nodes.procedure: The freshly made NiFe-LDH samples were separately immersed in 1 mM, 3 mM, and 5 mM WCl6 ethanol/water solutions (ethanol/water volume ratio of 1:1) at 25°C for 3 h, and the solutions were stirred by a magnetic stirring device during immersion. After immersion treatment, the samples were washed and dried to obtain NiFeW1-LDHs, NiFeW3-LDHs, and NiFeW5-LDHs.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pristine NiFe-LDHs display uniform and consistent growth of layered nanosheets. NiFeW3-LDHs show different sizes of nanopores on the surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The pristine NiFe-LDHs display uniform and consistent growth of layered nanosheets (Fig. 2a). ... there are different sizes of nanopores on the NiFeW3-LDHs surface (Fig. 2c)

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms nanosheet structure of NiFeW3-LDH. HRTEM exhibits polycrystalline phases with good lattice fringes and amorphous phases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM image confirms the nanosheet structure of NiFeW3-LDH (Fig. 2e), and the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image exhibits that the nanosheets are composed of polycrystalline phases ... and amorphous phases

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX elemental mappings illustrate that Ni, Fe, W, and O elements are homogeneously distributed on NF for NiFeW3-LDHs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the corresponding energy dispersive X-ray (EDX) elemental mappings of NiFeW3-LDHs illustrate that the Ni, Fe, W, and O elements are homogeneously distributed on NF (Fig. S2)

nodes.characterization_summary: Strong characteristic peaks of Ni foam are detected. Hydroxide phase not observed due to lower contents of NiFe and NiFeW hydroxides.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Strong characteristic peaks of Ni foam are detected in the XRD patterns of the samples (Fig. 3a). However, due to the lower contents of NiFe and NiFeW hydroxides ... the hydroxide phase is not observed

nodes.characterization_summary: Broad peak at 3379 cm^{-1} for -OH stretching, 1629 cm^{-1} for bending vibration of interlayer water, 1359 cm^{-1} for CO3^{2-} asymmetric stretching.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The broad and strong absorption peak at 3379 cm^{-1} belongs to the stretching vibration of -OH interlayer water molecules, and the relatively weak absorption peak at 1629 cm^{-1} ... The asymmetric stretching vibration of CO3^{2-} is observed at 1359 cm^{-1}

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p_{3/2} at 855.5 eV and 2p_{1/2} at 873.2 eV for NiFe-LDHs, positive shift ~0.3 eV for NiFeW3-LDHs. Fe 2p_{3/2} at 712.2 eV and 2p_{1/2} at 725.5 eV indicating Fe^{3+}. W 4f_{7/2} at 35.2 eV and 4f_{5/2} at 37.3 eV for W^{6+}. O 1s Vo peak area ratio 39.6% in NiFeW3-LDHs vs 33.1% in NiFe-LDHs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni 2p spectrum of (NiFe-LDHs) show spin-orbital peaks at 855.5 and 873.2 eV ... the peak position of Ni 2p ... for NiFeW3-LDHs displays a positive shift (~0.3 eV) ... The Fe 2p spectrum of NiFe-LDHs has two main peaks at 712.2 and 725.5 eV ... the W 4f spectrum shows two spin-orbital peaks at 37.3 eV (W 4f_{5/2}) and 35.2 eV (W 4f_{7/2}) ... The peak area ratio of Vo in NiFeW3-LDHs (39.6%) is higher than those of NiFe-LDHs (33.1%)

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR spectral intensity of NiFeW3-LDHs much higher than other samples, indicating W content influences Vo concentration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the EPR spectral intensity of NiFeW3-LDHs is much higher than those of NiFe-LDHs, NiFeW1-LDHs, and NiFeW5-LDHs (Fig. S4), indicating that the W content influences the Vo concentration

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental ratios: NiFe-LDHs (Ni65Fe35), NiFeW1-LDHs (Ni61Fe32W7), NiFeW3-LDHs (Ni58Fe30W12), NiFeW5-LDHs (Ni55Fe27W18).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The content ratios of metal elements in each sample were determined by inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). The elemental ratios in NiFe-LDHs, NiFeW1-LDHs, NiFeW3-LDHs, and NiFeW5-LDHs were Ni65Fe35, Ni61Fe32W7, Ni58Fe30W12, and Ni55Fe27W18

nodes.characterization_summary: Cdl values: NiFe-LDHs (14.36 mF cm^{-2}), NiFeW1-LDHs (17.18 mF cm^{-2}), NiFeW3-LDHs (22.11 mF cm^{-2}), NiFeW5-LDHs (18.82 mF cm^{-2}).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The fitting curves of iE versus ν and the corresponding double-layer capacitance (Cdl) values are illustrated in Fig. 5a and Table 1, respectively. The Cdl value of the optimized NiFeW3-LDHs is ~1.5 times that of NiFe-LDHs

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeW3-LDHs shows lowest Rct (0.20 Ω cm^{-2}), Rf (0.045 Ω cm^{-2}), highest Qdl (0.12 S s^{-1} cm^{-2}).
nodes.evidence_snippet: NiFeW3-LDHs with the best OER electrocatalytic activity demonstrate the lowest Rf and Rct and the highest Qdl
